analysis_steps.goal: Perform uv-plane strong lens modelling and pixelised source reconstruction

method.value: Semi-linear inversion (SLI) directly on visibilities in the uv-plane using PyAutoLens, PyNUFFT, and PyLops, fitting elliptical power-law mass density profiles (1 for galaxy-scale, 2 for group-scale) plus optional external shear, first with magnification-adapted source pixelisation and then brightness-adapted source pixelisation.

evidence.loc: The semi-linear inversion method in the uv-plane
evidence.quote: We used the source inversion method implemented within `PyAutoLens` (cite: Nightingale2021) which is based on the operator approach described within (cite: powell).

evidence.loc: The semi-linear inversion method in the uv-plane
evidence.quote: We first reconstructed the background source using a source plane pixelisation adapted to the lens magnification. This magnification-based fit was then used to initialise a new search of parameter space with a source plane that adapted to the brightness of the reconstructed source (cite: Nightingale2015; Nightingale2018).
We have used the elliptical power-law density profile, which is a generalised form of the singular isothermal ellipsoid that is commonly used to fit strong lens profiles (cite: keeton2001catalog).

key_parameters.value: Constant-weight gradient regularisation; 6 to 14 lens mass model parameters plus regularisation and number of source pixels

evidence.loc: The semi-linear inversion method in the uv-plane
evidence.quote: We adopted a gradient regularisation scheme, analogous to that which is described in (cite: warren_dye), with a constant weight for the source plane due to it’s simplicty and to not add more computational costs to an already expensive procedure.

evidence.loc: The semi-linear inversion method in the uv-plane
evidence.quote: The mass model parameters, along with the source plane parameters (regularisation, number of source plane pixels), were fully optimised throughout the lens modelling procedure.
For single lens systems there are six lens model parameters (eight when including external shear) and 12 lens model parameters (14 when including external shear) in the case of group-scale lenses.

assumptions.value: Elliptical power-law surface mass density profile (1 or 2 components) with optional external shear

evidence.quote: When it improves the Bayesian evidence, an external shear component is included to compensate for the influence of line of sight galaxies that may be outside our field of view.

analysis_steps.goal: Compute source magnification profiles and total magnification factors

method.value: Rank source plane pixels above a surface brightness threshold by flux density and compute the ratio of lensed image-plane flux (within the image-plane mask) to source-plane flux, repeating 100 times with randomised source plane pixelisation to average.

evidence.quote: Working down a list of source plane pixels, above a surface brightness threshold, ranked by flux density (i.e the product of their reconstructed surface brightness and area), the reconstructed image and average magnification was computed.
This process was repeated 100 times using a randomised source plane pixelisation for each, to produce an averaged magnification profile.

The total magnification is computed by calculating the flux in the source plane (for pixels above a surface brightness threshold) and the flux in the image plane due to the lensed image of the source plane pixels.

key_parameters.value: 100 realisations of randomised source plane pixelisation; surface brightness threshold; image plane mask

evidence.quote: This process was repeated 100 times using a randomised source plane pixelisation for each, to produce an averaged magnification profile.
Only the flux lying within the image plane mask contributes to the image plane flux and thus the total magnification.

validation.value: Comparison of magnification factors with previous literature models where available (e.g. H-ATLAS J083051.0+013225)

evidence.quote: They infer a magnification factor $\mu = 6.9 \pm 0.6$, which is in agreement with the magnification we find with our best fit model of $\mu = 6.7 \pm 0.5$.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit demagnified multi-wavelength SEDs and derive intrinsic dust mass, IR luminosity, gas mass, and SFR

method.value: Demagnify observed sub-mm/mm photometry by total magnification factor, fit rest-frame photometry with both a single-temperature optically thick SED and a dual-temperature optically thin SED, integrate the optically thin SED from 3 to 1100 um for L_IR, compute dust mass bounds using 873 um flux, H2 gas mass via scaling relations, and SFR from L_IR.

evidence.quote: To achieve this, we have demagnified the sub-mm photometry (see Table [\[tab:photometry\]](#tab:photometry)) by the total source magnification factors given in Table [\[tab:sources\]](#tab:sources), taking into account the uncertainties on our magnification values.
With the source redshifts given in Table [\[tab:redshifts\]](#tab:redshifts), we fitted the rest-frame photometry with two Spectral Energy Distributions (SEDs).

The best fit parameters for these SEDs can be found in Table [\[tab:sources\]](#tab:sources), along with the demagnified luminosity of the sources, computed by integrating the optically thin SED from 3-1100 $\mu$m.

findings_qualitative.value: Four systems are well described as galaxy-galaxy scale strong lenses (single power-law profile), and three as group-scale lenses (two power-law profiles).

evidence.quote: Four of these systems are galaxy-galaxy scale strong lenses, which are well described by a single power-law mass profile, whilst the remaining three are group-scale lenses, which have been successfully fitted with two power-law mass profiles.

findings_qualitative.value: Most of the modelled foreground lensing galaxies have power-law mass density slopes close to isothermal (alpha ~ 2), though some show significant deviations.

evidence.quote: The majority of our lens models have mass density slopes close to isothermal, but some systems show significant differences.
We have fitted smooth power-law density profiles (and in some cases two) for each of the lensing systems, and found that most of the lenses are close to isothermal.

findings_qualitative.value: All seven lensed sub-mm sources have SFR-to-dust-mass ratios consistent with or exceeding the mean ratio for high-redshift SMGs and local ULIRGs.

evidence.quote: We find that these sub-millimetre sources all have ratios of star formation rate to dust mass that is consistent with or in excess of the mean ratio for high-redshift sub-millimetre galaxies and low redshift ultra-luminous infrared galaxies.
Using the midpoint of this range to calculate the SFR to dust mass ratio, we find that all seven of our sources lie above the mean ratio for the SMG/ULIRG population as described in (cite: rowlands).

findings_qualitative.value: In the combined sample of 13 strongly lensed SMGs (combining this work with Dye et al. 2018), 9 out of 13 sources are visually classified as having disturbed morphologies.

evidence.quote: 9 of the 13 galaxies in our sample are visually classified as being disturbed, with at least two of them having evidence of being mergers (H-ATLAS J142935.3-002836, H-ATLAS J083051.0+01322).

claims.hypothesis: Foreground galaxy-scale and group-scale lenses in this sample have mass density profiles close to isothermal.
claims.experiment: Fit elliptical power-law surface mass density profiles (1 or 2 components) with optional external shear directly to ALMA Band 7 visibilities using PyAutoLens and DYNESTY.
claims.result: Power-law indices alpha range from 1.64 +/- 0.04 to 2.37 +/- 0.01 across the 10 modelled lens components, with most clustering near alpha ~ 2.0.
claims.finding: The majority of the lens models have mass density slopes close to isothermal, with some systems showing significant deviations.

evidence.quote: The majority of our lens models have mass density slopes close to isothermal, but some systems show significant differences.
We have fitted smooth power-law density profiles (and in some cases two) for each of the lensing systems, and found that most of the lenses are close to isothermal.

claims.hypothesis: Bright Herschel-selected lensed sub-mm galaxies exhibit elevated star formation efficiency (ratios of SFR to dust mass and H2 gas mass) compared to typical SMGs and ULIRGs.
claims.experiment: Demagnify multi-wavelength sub-mm/mm photometry using the inferred lens magnifications and fit optically thick and two-temperature optically thin SEDs to derive L_IR, SFR, M_d, and M_gas.
claims.result: All seven sources lie on or above the mean SFR-to-dust-mass and SFR-to-gas-mass relations, showing a factor of 6 increase in SFE over the SMG/ULIRG relation and a factor of 50 over z < 0.5 H-ATLAS galaxies.
claims.finding: The sources have higher than expected luminosities and SFRs for their dust/gas masses, consistent with elevated star formation efficiency, selection bias toward bright Herschel sources, or unquantified AGN contamination.

evidence.quote: Fitting a line parallel to the SMG/ULIRG relation shown in Fig. [\[fig:sfr_dm\]](#fig:sfr_dm), treating the range of dust masses as the 1-$\sigma$ error, we find an increase in SFE by a factor of 6 when compared with the value implied by the SMG/ULIRG relation from (cite: rowlands).
Using the midpoint of this range to calculate the SFR to dust mass ratio, we find that all seven of our sources lie above the mean ratio for the SMG/ULIRG population as described in (cite: rowlands).

claims.hypothesis: The combined Herschel-selected lensed SMG sample has higher effective dust temperatures than ALESS SMGs and local HERUS ULIRGs.
claims.experiment: Compare median L_IR and optically thick effective dust temperature of the combined 13-galaxy sample (this work plus Dye et al. 2018) against ALESS and HERUS.
claims.result: The combined sample has median L_IR = (5.1 +/- 2.5) x 10^12 L_sun and median T = 59 +/- 3 K, compared to T = 31 +/- 1 K for ALESS and T = 38 +/- 3 K for HERUS.
claims.finding: The sample exhibits significantly higher dust temperatures than ALESS and HERUS, which may reflect extreme SFRs and selection effects from targeting the brightest 500 um Herschel sources.

evidence.quote: The median dust temperature of our sample is significantly higher at $T = 59 \pm 3$K.

The high dust temperatures can be interpreted as a product of the extreme SFRs present in our sample, though it is important to bear in mind that the significance of these results are likely explained by the combination selection effects due to our observing of the brightest galaxies detected by Herschel and the sample of ALESS galaxies being selected at 870$\mu m$.

why_this_data.value: High-resolution (~0.12 arcsec) ALMA Band 7 observations combined with strong gravitational lensing magnification probe compact physical scales in the brightest 500 um Herschel-selected SMGs at z > 1.

evidence.quote: High-resolution sub-mm follow-up observations allow for precision lensing analyses, greatly benefiting our characterisation of source properties sensitive to the lens model, such as the intrinsic luminosity, star formation rate and gas and dust masses.

The observation targets for the original ALMA programme were selected from the H-ATLAS and HeLMS surveys for having the brightest 500 $\mu\mathrm{m}$ flux densities and with spectroscopic redshifts \> 1.

why_this_method.value: Modelling visibilities directly in the uv-plane using NUFFT operators avoids bias from spatially correlated image-plane noise caused by incomplete uv-coverage, while constant-weight gradient regularisation keeps computational cost manageable.

evidence.quote: The benefit of working in the image plane is that the task is significantly less computationally expensive, however, due to the incomplete coverage of the uv-plane, spatially correlated noise is introduced which can in principle bias the inferred lens model.
Working directly with the visibility data avoids this problem at the cost of longer modelling times.

evidence.loc: The semi-linear inversion method in the uv-plane
evidence.quote: We adopted a gradient regularisation scheme, analogous to that which is described in (cite: warren_dye), with a constant weight for the source plane due to it’s simplicty and to not add more computational costs to an already expensive procedure.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Image-plane lens modelling of CLEANed images (rejected in favour of direct uv-plane visibility modelling to avoid correlated noise bias).

evidence.quote: In this work we have opted to model the visibility data directly rather than to work with CLEANed image plane data.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Direct Fourier Transform (DFT) for uv-plane inversion (replaced by NUFFT via PyNUFFT due to memory and computational cost).

evidence.loc: The semi-linear inversion method in the uv-plane
evidence.quote: For this reason, a Direct Fourier Transform (DFT) is replaced by a non-uniform Fast Fourier Transform (NUFFT), constructed out of a series of operators.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: More complex source-plane regularisation schemes (rejected in favour of constant-weight gradient regularisation for simplicity and lower computational cost).

evidence.loc: The semi-linear inversion method in the uv-plane
evidence.quote: We adopted a gradient regularisation scheme, analogous to that which is described in (cite: warren_dye), with a constant weight for the source plane due to it’s simplicty and to not add more computational costs to an already expensive procedure.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Including more than two lens mass profiles for group-scale systems (rejected based on acceptable fits and optical/near-IR imaging).

evidence.quote: We find that in all cases this is sufficient to provide acceptable fits to the data and through the use of optical/near-IR imaging, we see no indication of more than two lenses being required to produce an accurate model.

how_they_decided_enough.value: External shear was included when it improved the Bayesian evidence; optical/near-IR imaging and residuals showed no need for more than two lens mass profiles; 100 random pixelisations were averaged for magnification profiles.

evidence.quote: When it improves the Bayesian evidence, an external shear component is included to compensate for the influence of line of sight galaxies that may be outside our field of view.

We find that in all cases this is sufficient to provide acceptable fits to the data and through the use of optical/near-IR imaging, we see no indication of more than two lenses being required to produce an accurate model.
This process was repeated 100 times using a randomised source plane pixelisation for each, to produce an averaged magnification profile.

limitations_admitted.value: Possible AGN contribution to the infrared luminosity is not quantified and could bias inferred star formation rates to higher values.

evidence.quote: The contribution to the infrared luminosity from possible AGN is not quantified and so could be biasing our star formation rates to higher values.
An unknown fraction of our sources could have their SFR over estimated due to significant contamination in the IR by strongly obscured AGN.

limitations_admitted.value: Selection bias toward the brightest 500 um Herschel sources may explain the extreme luminosities, dust temperatures, and SFR-to-dust-mass ratios.

evidence.quote: It is also important to note that this excess could be at least in part explained by selection bias, as we have chosen the brightest Herschel sources to follow-up on.

limitations_admitted.value: Large uncertainties in the dust mass absorption coefficient kappa_873 and the assumption of constant dust properties across the sample.

evidence.quote: The uncertainties in the dust mass absorption coefficient are known to be large, but a relative comparison between dust masses computed with this value is still valuable.
The same value of $\kappa_{873}$ was used for all of our galaxies, which assumes that the physical properties of the dust, such as grain size and density, are constant for our sample of galaxies.

limitations_admitted.value: Missing source redshift and PACS photometry for HeLMS J235331.9+031718 prevents constraining a warm dust component and requires assuming a redshift range of z = 2.0 - 3.7.

evidence.quote: There is no redshift measurement for this source and so we have opted to use the range of redshifts ($z \sim 2 - 3.7$) present in our sample to calculate redshift dependent quantities.
Without the PACS measurements and with the extra free parameters of the optically thin SED, it is not possible to meaningfully infer the presence of a warmer dust component.

limitations_admitted.value: Potential degeneracies between lens model parameters may cause deviations from an isothermal power-law slope.

evidence.quote: In some instances, there are significant deviations from an isothermal power-law slope, which may be due to degeneracies between parameters in our model or reflect the true nature of the lens, but we leave a more thorough explanation of this to further work.

limitations_admitted.value: Differential magnification across different dust temperature components is not accounted for in the single total magnification demagnification of the SEDs.

evidence.quote: A possible explanation for the large discrepancy in SFR is differential magnification of the source.

referee_caveats_inferred: Applying a single 873 um magnification factor across 100-1940 um photometry ignores differential magnification between compact warm dust and extended cold dust.
Lens redshifts are missing for two systems (HeLMS J234051.5-041938 and HeLMS J232439.5-043935), which limits physical interpretation of Einstein radii.
Multi-plane lensing effects are not modelled for H-ATLAS J083051.0+013225 despite its two deflectors lying at distinct redshifts (z = 0.626 and z = 1.002).
